title: App lifecycle and background execution
summary: An app moves between Not running, Inactive, Active, Background and Suspended. In the background you only get time through specific APIs; the system can kill a suspended app any time.
body: **States in simple words:** **Not running** - not started or killed. **Inactive** - on screen but not receiving events (incoming call, Control Center pulled down). **Active** - on screen, receiving touches. **Background** - not visible, still running code for a short while. **Suspended** - in memory but frozen; can be killed without notice to free memory.

**Where you hear about it:** with scenes, UI events go to `UISceneDelegate` (`sceneDidBecomeActive`, `sceneDidEnterBackground`) or SwiftUI `scenePhase`. Process events (launch, push token) stay in `UIApplicationDelegate`. iPad can have multiple scenes (windows) of one app.
**What to do on background:** save user data and state, pause timers and media (unless background audio), release big resources.

**Getting background time:** `beginBackgroundTask` (~30 seconds to finish something; always end it). `BGAppRefreshTask` (short refresh, system decides when). `BGProcessingTask` (minutes, e.g. while charging). `BGContinuedProcessingTask` (iOS 26, user-started work like exports, with system progress UI). Background `URLSession` for transfers. Silent push (`content-available`) for a brief wake-up. Special modes: audio, location, VoIP, Bluetooth.
**The system decides:** background tasks depend on battery, Low Power Mode, how often the user opens the app, and the Background App Refresh setting. Never rely on them for critical work.
keyPoints: States: not running, inactive, active, background, suspended.
Scene delegate/scenePhase for UI lifecycle; app delegate for process-level events.
Save state when entering background; suspended apps can be killed silently.
Background time only via specific APIs: background tasks, BGTaskScheduler, background URLSession, push, special modes.
Background execution is opportunistic, not guaranteed.

code.caption: Scheduling an app refresh

mistakes: Not ending a `beginBackgroundTask` (the app is killed).
Expecting `applicationWillTerminate` to be called - it usually is not for suspended apps.
followups: **How do you test background tasks?** Pause in the debugger and run `e -l objc -- (void)[[BGTaskScheduler sharedScheduler] _simulateLaunchForTaskWithIdentifier:@"com.app.refresh"]`.
**Why didn't my background task run?** Low Power Mode, rarely used app, Background App Refresh disabled, or not registered before launch finished.
**What happens when a user force-quits the app?** Background refresh and silent pushes stop until the user opens the app again.
